types.necessity: L1.identity requires that a change to a customer does not make it a different customer; a value invariant across all of a customer's dated statements is required to express that persistence, which is exactly the identity mutation role.
types.parallel_assumption: Credible while the brokerage's customer number is never reassigned to a different customer; if a customer number were reused for a different customer this role would misidentify statements, which should trigger review.
types.review_trigger: the same customer_number value appears to identify two customers the business considers different

types.necessity: L1.identity requires that a change to an account does not make it a different account; a value invariant across all of an account's dated statements is required to express that persistence, which is exactly the identity mutation role.
types.parallel_assumption: Credible while the brokerage's account number is never reassigned to a different account; if an account number were reused for a different account this role would misidentify statements, which should trigger review.
types.review_trigger: the same account_number value appears to identify two accounts the business considers different

types.necessity: L1.history requires the moment a change took effect be kept beside the statement, and L1.as-of requires ordering statements by that moment to answer any as-of question; a dedicated effective-time value is indispensable to both. It belongs to one dated statement and is never replaced in place, which is exactly the per_statement mutation role.
types.parallel_assumption: Credible while every statement's effective moment can be determined at all; where a source supplies no moment of its own, this value cannot yet be assigned and as-of answers for that statement are unavailable.
types.review_trigger: a statement is recorded with no determinable effective moment, or two statements of the same identity report the same moment

types.necessity: L1.current-version defines the current statement as the one with no later statement and requires exactly one per customer or account; a flag recording that fact is indispensable to expose it without recomputation. It is a fact about that dated statement relative to the others, never edited in place on an existing statement, which is the per_statement mutation role, not mutable.
types.parallel_assumption: Credible as long as effective moments are known and ordered for every statement of a thing; if effective moments are missing, the current flag cannot be determined either.
types.review_trigger: more than one or zero statements of the same identity are flagged current

types.necessity: L1.owner-standing requires that an account's standing include its owner's standing, and L1.statement-content names 'which customer owns it' as part of what an account's dated statement carries; the account's statement must therefore carry which customer it belongs to so that customer's as-of statement can be found for the same moment. This value belongs to one dated statement and is never replaced in place, which is the per_statement mutation role.
types.parallel_assumption: Credible while every account statement's owning customer is knowable at the moment the statement is recorded; whether a change to the owner alone creates a new account statement is unresolved.
types.review_trigger: an account statement has no resolvable owning customer, or the owner recorded contradicts the customer entity's identity values

types.necessity: the clause requires any constructed scenario be labeled wherever it appears and never mixed into received records; a dedicated provenance value is indispensable to carry that label through the model. It belongs to one dated statement and is never replaced in place, which is the per_statement mutation role.
types.parallel_assumption: Credible while every constructed scenario is loaded only through its labeled source and every received record is loaded only through raw sources.
types.review_trigger: a statement sourced from a raw feed carries a constructed label, or a statement sourced from a labeled constructed feed carries none

types.necessity: L1.statement-content enumerates 'whether the customer is active or inactive' as part of the standing facts a customer's dated statement carries; a dedicated status value is indispensable to express that specific enumerated fact, distinct from tier. It belongs to one dated statement and is never replaced in place.
types.parallel_assumption: Credible while the brokerage's own status coding distinguishes exactly active and inactive states for a customer at the moment of a statement; a source that reports additional intermediate states would require this type to be reassessed.
types.review_trigger: a source reports a customer status value that is neither active nor inactive, or a customer statement has no determinable status where the clause requires one

types.necessity: L1.statement-content enumerates 'the customer's tier' as part of the standing facts a customer's dated statement carries; a dedicated tier value is indispensable to express that specific enumerated fact.
types.parallel_assumption: Credible while the brokerage records a single tier value per customer statement, consistent with a per_statement fact rather than a running total.
types.review_trigger: a customer statement reports more than one tier value, or a tier value outside the brokerage's known tier range

types.necessity: L1.statement-content enumerates 'whether the account is open or closed' as part of the standing facts an account's dated statement carries; a dedicated status value is indispensable to express that specific enumerated fact, distinct from tax treatment and ownership.
types.parallel_assumption: Credible while the brokerage's own status coding distinguishes exactly open and closed states for an account at the moment of a statement.
types.review_trigger: a source reports an account status value that is neither open nor closed, or an account statement has no determinable status where the clause requires one

types.necessity: L1.statement-content enumerates 'its tax treatment' as part of the standing facts an account's dated statement carries; a dedicated tax-treatment value is indispensable to express that specific enumerated fact.
types.parallel_assumption: Credible while the brokerage records a single tax-treatment value per account statement, consistent with a per_statement fact.
types.review_trigger: an account statement reports more than one tax-treatment value, or a value outside the brokerage's known tax-treatment codes

entities.grain: one dated statement about one customer, holding from its effective moment until superseded by a later statement of the same customer
entities.necessity: L1.identity requires the customer to be a persistent identified thing rather than a row that changes identity; L1.history requires every change kept beside the earlier one with its effective moment; L1.as-of requires the kept statements be ordered so any moment resolves to one of them — together these entail a versioned entity of dated statements about one identified customer. The single-current-statement requirement and the standing facts each statement carries are further specified, at the attribute level, by L1.current-version and L1.statement-content respectively.
entities.parallel_assumption: Credible while every recorded change to a customer is delivered as a new statement rather than an overwrite of a prior one.
entities.review_trigger: a customer's prior statement is found overwritten rather than superseded by a new one

attributes.name: customer_number
attributes.necessity: L1.identity requires a value that identifies which customer a statement is about and stays the same across that customer's changes; this attribute carries the identity type for exactly that purpose.
attributes.parallel_assumption: Credible while the brokerage's customer number is stable and unique per customer.
attributes.review_trigger: two statements with different customer_number values are claimed to be about the same customer, or vice versa

attributes.name: effective_from
attributes.necessity: L1.history requires the moment a change took effect be kept with the statement; L1.as-of requires that moment to determine which statement answers a query as of any time.
attributes.parallel_assumption: Credible where the source of this statement supplies its own moment of change; not yet derivable for incremental customer change records.
attributes.review_trigger: a customer statement has no source-supplied moment of change

attributes.name: is_current

derivation.rule: true when no statement of the same customer_number has a later effective_from than this one; false otherwise. Not received from any source, per L1.current-version's definition of the current statement as the one with no later statement.

attributes.necessity: L1.current-version requires exactly one current statement per customer, defined as the one with no later statement; this attribute exposes that fact directly.
attributes.parallel_assumption: Credible once every customer statement has a known effective_from to order it against the others.
attributes.review_trigger: zero or more than one statement of the same customer_number is flagged current

attributes.name: status
attributes.necessity: L1.statement-content requires a customer's dated statement to carry whether the customer is active or inactive; this attribute carries that fact directly on the statement.
attributes.parallel_assumption: Credible where the source of this statement supplies its active/inactive fact directly, or entails it through a stated code meaning: the historical action file entails it through the anchored meaning of action_type (NEW, UPDCUST: active; INACT: inactive), and an incremental customer change record supplies it directly through c_st_id, though the latter's effective moment is not yet resolvable (L1.hole.change-effective-time).
attributes.review_trigger: a customer statement is recorded with no determinable active/inactive fact from a source that is expected to supply or entail one

attributes.name: tier

derivation.rule: When the action producing this statement omits the customer's tier field (as INACT does; see sources-v1.json action_type_meanings.fields_present), L1.omitted-facts-stand holds that the omitted fact stands as it last stood: tier equals the value carried by this customer's immediately preceding statement. L1.identity holds that a change produces a new dated statement about the same customer, not a different one, and L1.history holds that a later statement sits beside the earlier one rather than overwriting it, so 'the immediately preceding statement of this customer' is well defined. A preceding statement is guaranteed to exist here: INACT's anchored meaning ('a customer becomes inactive') presupposes an existing customer, since only NEW first records a customer, so an INACT row is never a customer's first statement.

attributes.necessity: L1.statement-content requires a customer's dated statement to carry the customer's tier; this attribute carries that fact directly on the statement. Where the producing action omits this field (as INACT does), this attribute's own carried_forward_from_previous_statement derivation supplies it instead, per L1.omitted-facts-stand, L1.identity, and L1.history.
attributes.parallel_assumption: Credible where the source of this statement supplies its own tier fact directly, or, when the producing action omits it, per the carried-forward derivation; credible while an action's omission of tier is understood to mean the fact is unchanged rather than unknown. The preceding statement this derivation carries from is itself sourced from the historical action file only while incremental customer CDC content handoffs stay deferred under L1.hole.change-effective-time; should they be promoted to candidate, this derivation must be revisited for how it identifies the immediately preceding statement.
attributes.review_trigger: a customer statement has no determinable tier value from a source that is expected to supply or carry it forward

entities.grain: one dated statement about one account, holding from its effective moment until superseded by a later statement of the same account
entities.necessity: L1.identity, L1.history, and L1.as-of require the same versioned-and-identified shape as the customer entity: a persistent identified account with dated, kept, orderable statements. The single-current-statement requirement, the owning-customer link, and the standing facts each statement carries are further specified, at the attribute level, by L1.current-version, L1.owner-standing, and L1.statement-content respectively.
entities.parallel_assumption: Credible while every recorded change to an account is delivered as a new statement rather than an overwrite of a prior one.
entities.review_trigger: an account's prior statement is found overwritten rather than superseded by a new one

attributes.name: account_number
attributes.necessity: L1.identity requires a value that identifies which account a statement is about and stays the same across that account's changes; this attribute carries the identity type for exactly that purpose.
attributes.parallel_assumption: Credible while the brokerage's account number is stable and unique per account.
attributes.review_trigger: two statements with different account_number values are claimed to be about the same account, or vice versa

attributes.name: effective_from
attributes.necessity: L1.history requires the moment a change took effect be kept with the statement; L1.as-of requires that moment to determine which statement answers a query as of any time.
attributes.parallel_assumption: Credible where the source of this statement supplies its own moment of change; not yet derivable for incremental account change records.
attributes.review_trigger: an account statement has no source-supplied moment of change

attributes.name: is_current

derivation.rule: true when no statement of the same account_number has a later effective_from than this one; false otherwise. Not received from any source, per L1.current-version's definition of the current statement as the one with no later statement.

attributes.necessity: L1.current-version requires exactly one current statement per account, defined as the one with no later statement; this attribute exposes that fact directly.
attributes.parallel_assumption: Credible once every account statement has a known effective_from to order it against the others.
attributes.review_trigger: zero or more than one statement of the same account_number is flagged current

attributes.name: owning_customer_number

derivation.rule: When a statement's own source supplies no owning-customer value (as ce.account_changes does not), L1.omitted-facts-stand holds that a constructed change which does not mention the owner leaves the owner as it last stood: owning_customer_number equals the value carried by this account's immediately preceding statement. L1.identity holds that a change produces a new dated statement about the same account, not a different one, and L1.history holds that a later statement sits beside the earlier one rather than overwriting it, so 'this account's immediately preceding statement' is well defined. A constructed change sourced from ce.account_changes always has a previous statement to carry the owner from, because L1.constructed-scenarios' authorized clarification forbids a constructed scenario from introducing an account the brokerage does not have — it only changes something the received records already know — which inv.constructed_account_change_refers_to_known_account checks directly.

attributes.necessity: L1.owner-standing requires that an account's standing include its owner's standing, and L1.statement-content names 'which customer owns it' as part of what an account statement carries; this attribute names which customer that is so the customer's as-of statement can be looked up for the same moment. Where a statement's source does not supply this fact directly, this attribute's own carried_forward_from_previous_statement derivation supplies it instead, per L1.omitted-facts-stand, L1.identity, and L1.history.
attributes.parallel_assumption: Credible for whatever account statements exist; whether a change to the customer alone produces a new account statement carrying this same value is unresolved. The carried-forward derivation is credible while a change that does not mention the owner is understood to leave the owner unchanged rather than unknown; if the business intends otherwise, this derivation must be revisited.
attributes.review_trigger: an account statement's owning_customer_number does not match any customer_number known to the customer entity, or a constructed change is recorded as an account's first statement with no owning_customer_number determinable by this derivation

attributes.name: status
attributes.necessity: L1.statement-content requires an account's dated statement to carry whether the account is open or closed; this attribute carries that fact directly on the statement.
attributes.parallel_assumption: Credible where the source of this statement supplies its open/closed fact directly, or entails it through a stated code meaning: the historical action file entails it through the anchored meaning of action_type (NEW, ADDACCT, UPDACCT: open; CLOSEACCT: closed), the labeled constructed scenario supplies it directly through status_id, and an incremental account change record supplies it directly through ca_st_id though its effective moment is not yet resolvable (L1.hole.change-effective-time). Whether a CLOSEACCT-derived closed status remains accurate after any later, unrecorded reopening is bounded by L1.hole.closed-account-activity, not resolved by any handoff.
attributes.review_trigger: an account statement is recorded with no determinable open/closed fact from a source that is expected to supply or entail one, or a closed account is found to carry activity after its closing statement with no reopening action recorded

attributes.name: tax_treatment

derivation.rule: When the action producing this statement omits the account's tax-treatment field (as CLOSEACCT does; see sources-v1.json action_type_meanings.fields_present), L1.omitted-facts-stand holds that the omitted fact stands as it last stood: tax_treatment equals the value carried by this account's immediately preceding statement. L1.identity holds that a change produces a new dated statement about the same account, not a different one, and L1.history holds that a later statement sits beside the earlier one rather than overwriting it, so 'the immediately preceding statement of this account' is well defined. A preceding statement is guaranteed to exist here: CLOSEACCT's anchored meaning ('an account is closed') presupposes an existing account, since only NEW or ADDACCT first records an account, so a CLOSEACCT row is never an account's first statement.

attributes.necessity: L1.statement-content requires an account's dated statement to carry its tax treatment; this attribute carries that fact directly on the statement. Where the producing action omits this field (as CLOSEACCT does), this attribute's own carried_forward_from_previous_statement derivation supplies it instead, per L1.omitted-facts-stand, L1.identity, and L1.history.
attributes.parallel_assumption: Credible where the source of this statement supplies its own tax-treatment fact directly, or, when the producing action omits it, per the carried-forward derivation; credible while an action's omission of tax treatment is understood to mean the fact is unchanged rather than unknown. The preceding statement this derivation carries from is itself sourced from the historical action file only while incremental account CDC content handoffs stay deferred under L1.hole.change-effective-time; should they be promoted to candidate, this derivation must be revisited for how it identifies the immediately preceding statement.
attributes.review_trigger: an account statement has no determinable tax-treatment value from a source that is expected to supply or carry it forward

attributes.name: provenance
attributes.necessity: the clause requires a constructed scenario be labeled wherever it appears; this attribute carries that label on the account statement so it is never mistaken for a received record.
attributes.parallel_assumption: Credible while the only anchored constructed-scenario source for this job is account-level; no equivalent labeled source exists yet for customer statements.
attributes.review_trigger: an account statement sourced from a raw handoff carries a provenance value, or one sourced from the labeled constructed feed carries none

handoffs.necessity: L1.identity requires the customer's own number as its identity; this file's customer actions (NEW, UPDCUST, INACT) carry c_id as the brokerage's customer number on each such record.
handoffs.parallel_assumption: Credible while c_id values in this file are the brokerage's real customer numbers and not reused for different customers.
handoffs.review_trigger: a c_id value in this file is found reassigned to a different customer

handoffs.necessity: L1.history requires the moment a customer change took effect; action_ts is this file's own recorded moment for the action, unlike incremental change files which carry none of their own.
handoffs.parallel_assumption: Credible while action_ts records the moment the brokerage considers the change to have taken effect, not merely when it was received into this file.
handoffs.review_trigger: action_ts is found to record only receipt time, not effective time

handoffs.necessity: L1.statement-content requires a customer's dated statement to carry the customer's tier; this file is where a customer is first recorded or later actioned, and c_tier is the brokerage's own recorded tier value on each such record.
handoffs.parallel_assumption: Credible while c_tier on this file's rows records the tier the brokerage considers the customer to hold as of that row's action_ts.
handoffs.review_trigger: c_tier is found to record something other than the customer's tier as of the action

handoffs.necessity: L1.history requires every change to a customer be kept as a new dated statement, and this row's action_type marks exactly such a change (NEW, UPDCUST, INACT); L1.statement-content requires that statement carry whether the customer is active or inactive. chain/anchors/sources-v1.json states what each code means (NEW, UPDCUST: active; INACT: inactive) with its own cited authority; interpreting that stated meaning to populate this statement's status is reading a named reference the source defines, not inventing a mapping from action codes to status values.
handoffs.parallel_assumption: Credible while the anchored action_type_meanings (assumed authority, locator unverified; see sources-v1.json) correctly and exhaustively state NEW and UPDCUST as active and INACT as inactive for a customer statement; if the business states a different meaning for any of these codes, or a code outside this enumeration is observed, this handoff must be revisited. An action_type value outside the anchored set {NEW, UPDCUST, INACT} is held under L1.unknown-codes and yields no derived fact for this statement; per inv.unknown_codes_held, the row is reported naming the record and the code instead.
handoffs.review_trigger: a customer_mgmt_action row carries an action_type outside {NEW, UPDCUST, INACT}, or the business states a meaning for one of these codes that differs from the anchored one

handoffs.necessity: identity of the customer a change applies to must be carried even where the change's effective moment is not yet resolvable; c_id is this file's customer number.
handoffs.note: Deferred: raw.customer_cdc supplies no handoff of its own effective moment to logical.customer, a versioned entity, so a new dated statement cannot yet be projected from this source. Blocked by L1.hole.change-effective-time; see hole.change_effective_time.
handoffs.parallel_assumption: Credible while c_id values in this file match the same numbering as the historical load.
handoffs.review_trigger: the change-effective-time hole is resolved and this handoff can be promoted from deferred to candidate

handoffs.necessity: L1.statement-content requires a customer's dated statement to carry the customer's tier; this incremental file's c_tier supplies that value even while the statement's own effective moment is unresolved.

handoffs.parallel_assumption: Credible while c_tier on a customer change record names the tier the brokerage considers the customer to hold as of that change, independent of when the change is deemed to take effect.
handoffs.review_trigger: the change-effective-time hole is resolved and this handoff can be promoted from deferred to candidate

handoffs.review_trigger: a row from this source has an empty or missing provenance value

handoffs.parallel_assumption: Credible while status_id on a constructed account-change row states the open/closed status the scenario asserts the account holds as of that row's action_at, using the anchored status_codes (ACTV: active or open; INAC: inactive or closed). chain/anchors/sources-v1.json declares no vocabulary for ce.account_changes' own status_id; no meaning is invented for it here — per inv.unknown_codes_held, every row's status_id is itself a review trigger under L1.unknown-codes, reported naming the record and the code, and yields no derived fact beyond that report.
handoffs.review_trigger: a constructed account-change row carries a status_id value outside the anchored status_codes

handoffs.necessity: L1.statement-content requires an account's dated statement to carry its tax treatment; this labeled constructed source's own tax_status_id field supplies that value directly for scenarios built to test these rules, per L1.constructed-scenarios.
handoffs.parallel_assumption: Credible while tax_status_id on a constructed account-change row states the tax-treatment code the scenario asserts the account holds as of that row's action_at.
handoffs.review_trigger: a constructed account-change row carries a tax_status_id value the business does not recognize as a tax-treatment code

invariants.statement: For any customer_number, at most one statement has is_current = true, and if any statement of that customer exists, exactly one does.
invariants.necessity: L1.current-version states there is exactly one current statement per customer; this invariant is the direct restatement of that requirement over the is_current flag.
invariants.parallel_assumption: Holds as long as every statement of a customer is recorded with a determinable order; two statements claiming the same effective moment would make the current one undecidable.
invariants.review_trigger: two statements for the same customer_number report the same effective_from

invariants.statement: For any account_number, at most one statement has is_current = true, and if any statement of that account exists, exactly one does.
invariants.necessity: L1.current-version states there is exactly one current statement per account; this invariant is the direct restatement of that requirement over the is_current flag.
invariants.parallel_assumption: Holds as long as every statement of an account is recorded with a determinable order; two statements claiming the same effective moment would make the current one undecidable.
invariants.review_trigger: two statements for the same account_number report the same effective_from

invariants.statement: No two statements of the same customer_number both apply at the same moment; each moment in time is covered by at most one statement of that customer.
invariants.necessity: L1.history requires a later statement to sit beside the earlier one rather than overlapping it, and L1.as-of's requirement that any as-of question have exactly one answer holds only if statements partition time without overlap; this invariant is the direct restatement of that non-overlap requirement.
invariants.parallel_assumption: Holds while effective_from values are strictly ordered per customer; a duplicate or out-of-order effective_from would break the partition and should trigger review.
invariants.review_trigger: two statements of the same customer_number share an effective_from

invariants.statement: No two statements of the same account_number both apply at the same moment; each moment in time is covered by at most one statement of that account.
invariants.necessity: L1.history requires a later statement to sit beside the earlier one rather than overlapping it, and L1.as-of's requirement that any as-of question have exactly one answer holds only if statements partition time without overlap; this invariant is the direct restatement of that non-overlap requirement.
invariants.parallel_assumption: Holds while effective_from values are strictly ordered per account; a duplicate or out-of-order effective_from would break the partition and should trigger review.
invariants.review_trigger: two statements of the same account_number share an effective_from

invariants.statement: For any customer_number and any moment T, exactly one statement of that customer is the latest one effective at or before T, or none if T precedes the customer's first statement.
invariants.necessity: L1.as-of defines the as-of answer as the latest statement that took effect at or before the queried moment, which is unique only if statements are ordered and non-overlapping.
invariants.parallel_assumption: Holds under the no-overlap and ordering assumptions above; if they fail, an as-of question could have more than one candidate answer, which should trigger review.
invariants.review_trigger: an as-of query for a customer_number returns more than one candidate statement

invariants.statement: For any account_number and any moment T, exactly one statement of that account is the latest one effective at or before T, or none if T precedes the account's first statement.
invariants.necessity: L1.as-of defines the as-of answer as the latest statement that took effect at or before the queried moment, which is unique only if statements are ordered and non-overlapping.
invariants.parallel_assumption: Holds under the no-overlap and ordering assumptions above; if they fail, an as-of question could have more than one candidate answer, which should trigger review.
invariants.review_trigger: an as-of query for an account_number returns more than one candidate statement

invariants.statement: For any account_number and moment T, the account's as-of statement's owning_customer_number, looked up as of the same moment T in the customer entity, yields the customer's as-of statement; the account's as-of answer is not complete without it.
invariants.necessity: L1.owner-standing requires that an account's standing at a moment include how its customer stood at that same moment; L1.as-of supplies the same-moment lookup rule for both entities.
invariants.parallel_assumption: Holds as long as the account's owning_customer_number is known for the statement in question; where it is not yet derivable, the paired customer as-of answer cannot be produced either.
invariants.review_trigger: an account's as-of statement has no resolvable owning_customer_number, or the customer entity has no statement effective at the same moment

invariants.statement: Every account statement whose source is a labeled constructed scenario carries a non-null provenance value; no account statement sourced from received records carries a provenance value.
invariants.necessity: the clause requires constructed scenarios to be labeled wherever they appear and never mixed into received records; this invariant is the direct check of that requirement at the attribute level.
invariants.parallel_assumption: Holds as long as constructed scenarios are only ever loaded through the labeled ce.account_changes source and never through a raw source.
invariants.review_trigger: an account statement sourced from a raw handoff carries a non-null provenance value, or one sourced from ce.account_changes carries a null provenance value

invariants.statement: Every candidate-sourced statement of a customer carries a non-null status and a non-null tier; a versioned statement without either is content-free and fails L1.statement-content.
invariants.necessity: L1.statement-content requires a dated statement to carry the enumerated standing facts, not merely exist as an empty shell; this invariant is the direct check that status and tier are populated on every candidate-sourced statement, whether supplied directly by the source or carried forward under L1.omitted-facts-stand when the producing action omits the field.
invariants.parallel_assumption: Holds unconditionally for statements sourced from the historical action file: NEW and UPDCUST carry c_tier directly, and INACT omits it, so tier is carried forward from the customer's preceding statement under L1.omitted-facts-stand; status is entailed by the anchored action_type meaning on every one of NEW, UPDCUST, and INACT. Does not yet hold for a statement whose only source is an incremental customer change record, since that record's effective moment is not yet resolvable (L1.hole.change-effective-time) and its content handoffs remain deferred.
invariants.review_trigger: a customer statement from a source expected to supply or entail status or tier carries neither

invariants.statement: Every candidate-sourced statement of an account carries a non-null status and a non-null tax_treatment; a versioned statement without either is content-free and fails L1.statement-content.
invariants.necessity: L1.statement-content requires a dated statement to carry the enumerated standing facts, not merely exist as an empty shell; this invariant is the direct check that status and tax_treatment are populated on every candidate-sourced statement, whether supplied directly by the source or carried forward under L1.omitted-facts-stand when the producing action omits the field.
invariants.parallel_assumption: Holds unconditionally for statements sourced from the historical action file: NEW, ADDACCT, and UPDACCT carry ca_tax_st directly, and CLOSEACCT omits it, so tax_treatment is carried forward from the account's preceding statement under L1.omitted-facts-stand; status is entailed by the anchored action_type meaning on every one of NEW, ADDACCT, UPDACCT, and CLOSEACCT. Also holds unconditionally for statements sourced from the labeled constructed scenario ce.account_changes, which carries both status_id and tax_status_id directly on every row. Does not yet hold for a statement whose only source is an incremental account change record, since that record's effective moment is not yet resolvable (L1.hole.change-effective-time) and its content handoffs remain deferred.
invariants.review_trigger: an account statement from a source expected to supply or entail status or tax_treatment carries neither

invariants.statement: Every account statement sourced from the labeled constructed scenario ce.account_changes names an account_number that already has an earlier statement sourced from a received record; a constructed change never introduces an account the brokerage does not have.
invariants.necessity: L1.constructed-scenarios' authorized clarification states a constructed scenario changes something the received records already know and never introduces a customer, account, or trade the brokerage does not have; this invariant is the direct check of that requirement for ce.account_changes. It is also what guarantees that logical.account.owning_customer_number's carried_forward_from_previous_statement derivation always has a previous statement to carry from for a constructed change.
invariants.parallel_assumption: Holds while every constructed scenario used to test this job's rules is authored against an account already present in the received records, per the authorized clarification of L1.constructed-scenarios.
invariants.review_trigger: a constructed account-change row's account_id has no earlier statement sourced from a received record

invariants.statement: For every candidate-sourced customer statement produced by a historical action, status equals the anchored meaning of that action's action_type (NEW, UPDCUST: active; INACT: inactive); once an incremental customer change record's content handoffs are undeferred, status for a statement it produces equals that record's own c_st_id value.
invariants.necessity: L1.statement-content requires a customer statement to carry whether the customer is active or inactive; this invariant is the direct value-correctness check that the status this job hands off actually equals what its producing source states, under L1.history's requirement that the action be that statement's own producing change, rather than some other statement's value being substituted.
invariants.parallel_assumption: Holds while the anchored action_type_meanings correctly and exhaustively state NEW and UPDCUST as active and INACT as inactive; not yet checkable for a statement whose only source is an incremental customer change record, since that handoff remains deferred under L1.hole.change-effective-time.
invariants.review_trigger: a customer statement's status does not equal the anchored meaning of its producing action's action_type, or, once undeferred, does not equal its producing record's c_st_id

invariants.statement: For every candidate-sourced customer statement whose producing action carries c_tier (NEW, UPDCUST), tier equals that row's c_tier; for one whose producing action omits it (INACT), tier equals the value carried by the customer's immediately preceding statement, per L1.omitted-facts-stand.
invariants.necessity: L1.statement-content requires a customer statement to carry the customer's tier; this invariant is the direct value-correctness check that tier equals its producing row's own value where supplied, or the previous statement's value where the row omits it under L1.omitted-facts-stand, rather than some other statement's tier being substituted.
invariants.parallel_assumption: Holds for statements sourced from the historical action file, where NEW and UPDCUST carry c_tier directly and INACT's carried-forward value can be checked against the customer's immediately preceding statement; not yet checkable for a statement whose only source is an incremental customer change record, since that handoff remains deferred under L1.hole.change-effective-time.
invariants.review_trigger: a customer statement's tier does not equal its producing row's c_tier where carried, or does not equal the immediately preceding statement's tier where the row omits it

invariants.statement: For every candidate-sourced account statement produced by a historical action, status equals the anchored meaning of that action's action_type (NEW, ADDACCT, UPDACCT: open; CLOSEACCT: closed); for one produced by a labeled constructed scenario row, status equals that row's own status_id.
invariants.necessity: L1.statement-content requires an account statement to carry whether the account is open or closed; this invariant is the direct value-correctness check that the status this job hands off actually equals what its producing source states, whether a historical action interpreted under L1.history or a constructed scenario's own status_id under L1.constructed-scenarios, rather than some other statement's value being substituted.
invariants.parallel_assumption: Holds while the anchored action_type_meanings correctly and exhaustively state NEW, ADDACCT, and UPDACCT as open and CLOSEACCT as closed, and while ce.account_changes.status_id states the scenario's asserted status directly; not yet checkable for a statement whose only source is an incremental account change record, since that handoff remains deferred under L1.hole.change-effective-time.
invariants.review_trigger: an account statement's status does not equal the anchored meaning of its producing action's action_type, or does not equal its producing constructed row's status_id

invariants.statement: For every candidate-sourced account statement whose producing row carries a tax-treatment value directly (a historical action's ca_tax_st on NEW, ADDACCT, or UPDACCT, or a constructed scenario row's tax_status_id), tax_treatment equals that value; for one whose producing historical action omits it (CLOSEACCT), tax_treatment equals the value carried by the account's immediately preceding statement, per L1.omitted-facts-stand.
invariants.necessity: L1.statement-content requires an account statement to carry its tax treatment; this invariant is the direct value-correctness check that tax_treatment equals its producing row's own value where supplied directly, or the previous statement's value where a historical action omits it under L1.omitted-facts-stand, rather than some other statement's tax treatment being substituted.
invariants.parallel_assumption: Holds for statements sourced from the historical action file, where NEW, ADDACCT, and UPDACCT carry ca_tax_st directly and CLOSEACCT's carried-forward value can be checked against the account's immediately preceding statement, and for statements sourced from ce.account_changes, which carries tax_status_id directly on every row; not yet checkable for a statement whose only source is an incremental account change record, since that handoff remains deferred under L1.hole.change-effective-time.
invariants.review_trigger: an account statement's tax_treatment does not equal its producing row's directly supplied value, or does not equal the immediately preceding statement's tax_treatment where the producing action omits it

invariants.statement: For every candidate-sourced account statement whose producing historical action carries c_id, owning_customer_number equals that action's c_id; for one produced by a constructed scenario row, which carries no owner field, owning_customer_number equals the value carried by the account's immediately preceding statement, per L1.omitted-facts-stand.
invariants.necessity: L1.owner-standing and L1.statement-content require an account statement to name the customer who owns it; this invariant is the direct value-correctness check that owning_customer_number equals its producing historical action's own c_id where supplied, or the previous statement's value where a constructed scenario row omits it under L1.omitted-facts-stand, rather than some other statement's owner being substituted.
invariants.parallel_assumption: Holds for statements sourced from the historical action file, whose account actions (NEW, ADDACCT, UPDACCT, CLOSEACCT) all carry c_id directly, and for statements sourced from ce.account_changes, whose carried-forward value can be checked against the account's immediately preceding statement, guaranteed to exist by L1.constructed-scenarios and inv.constructed_account_change_refers_to_known_account; not yet checkable for a statement whose only source is an incremental account change record, since that handoff remains deferred under L1.hole.change-effective-time.
invariants.review_trigger: an account statement's owning_customer_number does not equal its producing historical action's c_id, or does not equal the immediately preceding statement's owning_customer_number where a constructed row omits the owner

invariants.statement: For every raw.customer_mgmt_action row this job consumes, action_type is one of the codes chain/anchors/sources-v1.json's action_type_meanings names (NEW, ADDACCT, UPDACCT, UPDCUST, CLOSEACCT, INACT); a row carrying any other value is reported as a violation naming the row and its action_type, and nothing is derived from it. chain/anchors/sources-v1.json declares no named vocabulary for ce.account_changes' own status_id field, so every ce.account_changes row's status_id is itself a review trigger under this invariant: it is reported naming the row and its status_id value, exactly as an unrecognized action_type would be, because no anchored vocabulary exists to check it against and none is invented here. This invariant only reports the row and the code; it says nothing about what happens to the record afterward.
invariants.necessity: L1.unknown-codes requires that a report carrying a code the brokerage's fixed vocabulary does not name is held for review and never interpreted, defaulted, or dropped, and that every job report such a record as a violation naming the record and the code. This job consumes raw.customer_mgmt_action rows, whose action_type it reads to populate customer and account status, and ce.account_changes rows, whose status_id it reads directly with no anchored vocabulary at all; this invariant is the direct, deterministic check that both are reported rather than silently interpreted, defaulted, or dropped.
invariants.parallel_assumption: Holds while chain/anchors/sources-v1.json's action_type_meanings remains the exhaustive, correct naming of raw.customer_mgmt_action's action_type codes; the ce.account_changes.status_id half of this invariant carries no such assumption, since no vocabulary is anchored for it to be correct or exhaustive about — it is a review trigger by default, not a value pending validation against a named set.
invariants.review_trigger: a raw.customer_mgmt_action row carries an action_type outside {NEW, ADDACCT, UPDACCT, UPDCUST, CLOSEACCT, INACT}, or any ce.account_changes row is consumed (its status_id is always the trigger, per the missing vocabulary)

sufficiency_groups.coverage_claim: Every source this job reads through a raw feed that reports a customer or account carries its own identity handoff into the customer_number or account_number attribute, typed with the identity mutation role, giving each entity the persistent, non-identity-changing value L1.identity requires. Because a versioned entity's statements must also be kept beside one another and be orderable for as-of resolution, this group also covers the entity-shape-level portion of L1.history and L1.as-of: the historical action file's own action_ts handoff makes both entities projectable as dated, ordered statements now; the incremental CDC files carry the same identity values but supply no effective moment of their own, so their identity handoffs into these versioned entities are deferred. The labeled constructed account scenario's own identity handoff is covered under sg.constructed-scenarios instead, since it is the more specific claim about that source. L1.identity also names a trade number, out of this job's scope (see job:trade-lifecycle). The attribute-level effective_from population and ordering invariants are covered by sg.history-asof; the current-flag mechanics by sg.current-version.

For every statement whose source carries its own moment of change (the historical action file's action_ts), effective_from is populated and the no-overlap and unique-answer invariants hold over it, satisfying L1.history's 'kept, with the moment it took effect' and L1.as-of's 'the latest one that took effect at or before it.' The labeled constructed account scenario's own effective_from handoff (action_at) is covered under sg.constructed-scenarios instead, since it is the more specific claim about that source. Incremental CDC records carry no moment of their own (a batch date is not an effective moment, per L1.hole.change-effective-time), so no effective_from handoff is created from them.
sufficiency_groups.gap: L1.hole.change-effective-time; also bounded by L1.hole.deletions, since what a deletion marker in an incremental change file means for a customer's or account's kept history is unresolved.

sufficiency_groups.coverage_claim: The is_current flag, true for exactly the statement of a customer or account with no later statement and false for every other, together with the single-current invariants, is a direct restatement of L1.current-version's 'exactly one current statement per customer and per account.' This determination depends on every statement's effective_from being known; where a statement's only source is an incremental CDC file, its order relative to the customer's or account's other statements is not yet resolvable, so its current-ness cannot yet be determined either.
sufficiency_groups.gap: L1.hole.change-effective-time; also bounded by L1.hole.deletions, since what a deletion marker means for which statement of a customer or account is current is unresolved.

sufficiency_groups.coverage_claim: Every account statement sourced from a feed that itself supplies the account's own effective moment carries the identity of its owning customer: directly, from the historical action file's own c_id (the incremental account CDC file's own c_id handoff is deferred pending its own effective-time hole); and, for a statement sourced from the labeled constructed scenario ce.account_changes, which carries no owner field of its own, from this same attribute's own carried_forward_from_previous_statement derivation under L1.omitted-facts-stand, which holds that a constructed change not mentioning the owner leaves it as it last stood. L1.identity and L1.history make 'the account's immediately preceding statement' well defined, and L1.constructed-scenarios together with inv.constructed_account_change_refers_to_known_account guarantee that a preceding statement exists to carry from. The account_asof_carries_customer_asof invariant requires that owning-customer value be used to pair the account's as-of answer with the customer's as-of answer at the same moment — exactly L1.owner-standing's 'an account's standing includes its owner's standing,' using L1.as-of's same-moment lookup rule. L1.statement-content additionally names 'which customer owns it' as part of what an account statement carries, which this same attribute satisfies. The inv.account_owner_matches_producing_source invariant additionally checks that owning_customer_number equals what its producing source states, directly or by carry-forward, rather than merely being non-null.
sufficiency_groups.gap: L1.hole.owner-change-reversions-account; also bounded by L1.hole.change-effective-time (the incremental account CDC file's owner handoff remains deferred pending its own effective moment) and L1.hole.deletions (what a deletion marker in that file means for owner-standing is unresolved).

sufficiency_groups.coverage_claim: For every customer statement sourced from the historical action file: tier is handed off directly from c_tier on NEW and UPDCUST rows, and carried forward from the customer's preceding statement under L1.omitted-facts-stand on INACT rows, which omit c_tier; status is derived from action_type on every one of NEW, UPDCUST, and INACT, since the anchored action_type_meanings state a status for each. Both standing facts L1.statement-content names for a customer are therefore populated for every statement this source produces, by direct handoff or carry-forward. For every account statement sourced from the historical action file: tax_treatment is handed off directly from ca_tax_st on NEW, ADDACCT, and UPDACCT rows, and carried forward from the account's preceding statement under L1.omitted-facts-stand on CLOSEACCT rows, which omit ca_tax_st; status is derived from action_type on every one of NEW, ADDACCT, UPDACCT, and CLOSEACCT. Both facts L1.statement-content names for an account are therefore populated for every statement this source produces; the owning-customer fact it also names is covered under sg.owner-standing instead, since it is the more specific claim about that attribute. For every account statement sourced from the labeled constructed scenario ce.account_changes — the one account source with no pending effective-time hole of its own — status and tax treatment are handed off directly from that source's own status_id and tax_status_id fields, present on every row, so this fully projectable source's statements are not content-free. The incremental CDC files carry the same tier, tax-treatment, and status values but supply no effective moment of their own, so all of their content handoffs into these versioned entities remain deferred. Four value-correctness invariants (inv.customer_status_matches_producing_source, inv.customer_tier_matches_producing_source, inv.account_status_matches_producing_source, inv.account_tax_treatment_matches_producing_source) additionally check that each populated value equals what its producing source states, directly or by carry-forward, rather than merely being non-null.
sufficiency_groups.gap: L1.hole.change-effective-time bounds the deferred CDC-sourced handoffs above, which cannot yet be projected. Separately, L1.hole.closed-account-activity bounds the account status this group now derives from action_type: a CLOSEACCT statement's closed status is not revised by this model if the account's activity later resumes without a recorded reopening action. Also bounded by L1.hole.deletions: what a deletion marker in an incremental change file means for the standing facts it would otherwise carry is unresolved.

sufficiency_groups.coverage_claim: The handoffs drawing from the labeled ce.account_changes source that are members of this group establish this account statement's identity, effective time, and constructed label: account_id populates account_number and action_at populates effective_from, satisfying L1.identity's persistent-identity requirement and L1.history/L1.as-of's dated, ordered statement requirement for this source specifically; provenance populates the account statement's own provenance field, and only ever from this source, while no raw-sourced handoff ever populates it, satisfying L1.constructed-scenarios' 'labeled... wherever it appears' and 'never mixed into the received records.' The standing facts this source's rows also carry, status_id and tax_status_id, are populated by handoffs that are members of sg.statement-content instead, since content coverage is the more specific claim owned there; this group's coverage is limited to identity, history/as-of, and labeling for this source.

inv.unknown_codes_held is the direct and complete check, for this job, of L1.unknown-codes' requirement that an unnamed code be held for review and reported rather than interpreted, defaulted, or dropped: it covers the one coded field this job reads from a currently-projectable candidate source with an anchored vocabulary (raw.customer_mgmt_action.action_type) and the one coded field this job reads that has no anchored vocabulary at all (ce.account_changes.status_id), naming both explicitly rather than inventing a vocabulary for the second.
sufficiency_groups.gap: raw.customer_cdc.c_st_id and raw.account_cdc.ca_st_id are also coded fields this job reads, against the same anchored status_codes vocabulary, but their handoffs remain deferred under L1.hole.change-effective-time and derive no fact yet; this invariant does not yet check them, and must be extended to cover them once those handoffs are undeferred.

holes.question: When a customer's standing changes, does every account of that customer receive a new dated statement at that same moment, or only the customer?
Does a change recorded in an incremental customer or account change file take effect at the file's batch date, or at some other moment?

What does a deletion marker in an incremental account or customer change file mean for that thing's history, its current statement, the owner-standing an account carries, and the standing facts a statement carries?

Activity appears on accounts this job would derive as closed (via a CLOSEACCT action recorded years earlier). Is that a data error, an unrecorded reopening the historical action file omits, or does a closed account still own activity? Until answered, an account's status history derived by this job may be incomplete: once a statement's status is derived as closed, this model does not revise it even if later activity suggests the account reopened.

Does this job need to know which incremental file first delivered a fact? None of this job's clauses (L1.identity, L1.history, L1.as-of, L1.current-version, L1.owner-standing, L1.statement-content, L1.constructed-scenarios) ask this. Dismissed as not applicable to job:ownership-history unless the business states a clause that requires it.
